title: I Took the University Lost-and-Found Tag to the Desk That Wore My Jacket

parts.text: I described my jacket at 2:06 p.m. and the desk attendant was wearing it. The lost-and-found tag on the sleeve, still attached, said: HOLD 30 DAYS. STAFF MAY NOT WEAR INVENTORY. I was twenty, student, holding a photo of the unique patch. Attendant Jules said, "It's cold at the desk." I pointed at the tag. They zipped higher. "Cold is operations." I photographed the tag on a moving sleeve, the policy poster, and my photo. Then I asked campus security to match the patch. At 2:11 security asked why Jules's name was on a worn-inventory ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Security can see the hold tag on a staff sleeve against the may-not-wear poster.

social.video_title: Lost-and-found was wearing my jacket — Part 1/2
social.description: Unique patch, a cold desk, and a 30-day tag still on the sleeve. I called security. Would you have described it nicer?

parts.text: Jules called it a fit check until security matched the patch. I printed the ticket, the poster, and the photo. I got the jacket. Jules wore their own hoodie and told the counter the poster was always about optics. Optics is a word desks use when a patch exists. Hold policy now has a second line: COLD BUYS A SWEATER. I walk warm. Jules inventories. The bin finally has coats that stay still.

social.video_title: Cold buys a sweater, not inventory — Part 2/2
social.description: Worn-inventory ticket, my patch back, and a second line on the poster. Was operations ever my sleeve?
